review.summary: Charcoal from the main room of Amaknak Bridge’s Structure 7 dates to approximately 1280–820 BCE. The interval is the sample’s dating range, not evidence that the room was used continuously for all those years.
review.limitations: Single wood-charcoal determination; old-wood and depositional associations require caution. No language or resident population assigned.
review.discussion: Calibrated uncertainty is retained in full. The excavators consider an occupation hiatus possible; chronological overlap is not proof that all houses were contemporaneous.
